items.summary: Some terms does not have an official translation yet and will stay in english in this presentation The Blackbird Clan is a group of outlaw Swarowls from the world of Zerzur. These bandits live in the Almaz region, where they lie in wait, re
items.content:
Some terms does not have an official translation yet and will stay in english in this presentation

The Blackbird Clan is a group of outlaw Swarowls from the world of Zerzur. These bandits live in the Almaz region, where they lie in wait, ready to plunder anyone who attempts to pass through the area. They are led by Mary’Lyn Monrowl, who has ensured the clan’s prosperity in these troubled times.

Instances linked to the Blackbird Clans

Gustwind Canyon

This windswept canyon is the rugged, secret hideout of the Blackbird Clan and serves as Mary’Lyn Monrowl’s base of operations. From here, she orchestrates her raids and plots her revenge against Zerzur.

Egglektra’s Nest

Egglektra is the largest Volture in the Obral region. She was formerly owned by a noble Zerzur family, but was stolen by the Blackbird Clan and used as a secret weapon against their enemies.

Master Thunder abilities

By fighting the Blackbird Clan in the world and in the dungeons, you’ll get access to their specific loot and weapons. Using their weapon will unlock the mastery of thunder for you. Whether it is through the Zerzurian Cleavers (dual axe for Warrior and rogue), the Eye of the storm (scepter for Mage and Priest) or the Flying blades of the tormented bird (thrown weapon for Rogue and Priest) On top of those, you'll also get to look cool and intimidating while using a brand new weapon type! Introducing, the Blade of the Four Winds (katana for Warrior and Rogue)

items.title: Nominate Farever for “Better With Friends” at the Steam Awards!
items.summary: Good day, Farseekers! The Steam Awards are celebrating their 10th anniversary , and we’d love your help to make Farever part of the celebration! If your favourite adventures in Siagarta have been shared with friends, consider nominating Far
items.content:
Good day, Farseekers!

The Steam Awards are celebrating their 10th anniversary, and we’d love your help to make Farever part of the celebration! If your favourite adventures in Siagarta have been shared with friends, consider nominating Farever for the “Better With Friends” Award.

Gather your party. Someone will know the way. Probably.

Old friends, new faces, or that one Farseeker who confidently leads everyone in the wrong direction: every party brings something special to Siagarta.

Your feedback helped us give those shared adventures a boost with the Call to Glory update:

  • Friend lists and additional chat channels, because finding a good teammate deserves a more reliable follow-up than “hope we bump into each other again!”

    [/*]

  • Improved group rewards and loot, because friendship is priceless, but shiny loot certainly helps.

    [/*]

  • Reviving allies during boss battles, because “I had it under control” deserves a second chance.

    [/*]

  • New emotes and an updated group HUD, so you can express yourself and keep an eye on your party. Especially the friend who wandered off. Again.

    [/*]

Good friends. Great adventures. Questionable plans.

Farever keeps growing, and your feedback helps shape what comes next! We’ll keep working on more ways to bring Farseekers together for glorious victories, unexpected friendships, and the occasional “I thought you were healing!”

If Farever has given you stories your party still laughs about, nominate us for “Better With Friends” at the Steam Awards!

Thank you for every adventure, every suggestion, and every friend you’ve convinced that “just one more dungeon” was a good idea.

See you in Siagarta, Farseekers!

The Farever Team.

New Area - The Obral Summit

The Obral Summit is a mountainous region located north of Eksod. In it you’ll be able to use unique traversal option via sparkfused rails to move vertically across the terrain.

Get your character to a new level

Thank you for playing our game, giving us your feedback, whether you follow along in the public test or wait for the official release. This update bring a lot of new things and we’re looking forward to your experience in it!

items.title: Farever Shop Info and Update
items.summary: Hey Farseekers! As we continue supporting the growth of Farever with new content, features, and ongoing performance improvements, we are getting ready to test the opening of the Farever shop, where you will find purchasable cosmetic items,
items.content:
Hey Farseekers! As we continue supporting the growth of Farever with new content, features, and ongoing performance improvements, we are getting ready to test the opening of the Farever shop, where you will find purchasable cosmetic items, helping us further support the development of the game. The Farever shop is now available on the Public Test Branch, with a first set of items. Purchases made on the Public Test Branch will make the items available in your collections on all live servers you’re playing on.

How the Shop Works

To access the shop, you can go to the menu by pressing “escape” and checking the “Shop” option. Here you will have different tabs for the different sets. Here you will find unique mounts, pets, gliders, and, in the future, more cool-looking cosmetics. These items are optional and do not have any gameplay impact or give any advantage to players who purchase them (except looking great). Once purchased, these items directly join your Collection tab. They are accessible for all of your characters across regions and cannot be traded away. Shop items can be purchased using Spark Coins, a separate currency available in packs directly in the same Shop. We are currently testing this feature in the Public Test Branch. You can already test it yourself, as all purchases done in the PTR will be available directly to you in the live version as well! To join the Public Test Branch:
  • Right-click on Farever in your Steam Library
  • Select Properties → Betas
  • Choose the “Public Beta Branch”
 The Farever Shop will grow alongside the game, helping support ongoing development and server maintenance, without taking priority over new updates, quality-of-life features, or performance improvements.

New set in the shop - Lizhazard Bundle

In the shop, you can currently find the Lizhazard Bundle. It contains all the elements you can expect in future sets for the shop. A glider, a pet, and a mount. Here they are:
  • Lizhazard Kodog - Kodogs are a clever cross between a large lizard and a dog. They are incredibly affectionate but can change their mood in a matter of seconds. When they shed, they leave enough skin and fur behind to accidentally duplicate themselves.
  • Lizhazard Saladmander - The dorsal fur of Lizhazard Saladmanders blooms in the fall and sometimes bursts into flames during mating displays. Some careless males have even ended up charred to a crisp on nights of passionate love.
  • Lizhazard Thunderhawk - Contrary to what their name might suggest, Thunderhawks have nothing in common with either thunder or hawks. They can glide but not fly, and they are terrified of bad weather. Biologists are sometimes seized by a creative frenzy when it comes to naming creatures.
The previous Early Access Bundle is still available for free in the shop, and will remain until the end of early access! New cosmetic items will be updated in the shop alongside updates to the game in the future. We want to thank you for supporting us during this Early Access period. We also want to remind you that you can also support the game simply by being a part of the community, leaving in-game feedback to help us improve your experience and by leaving a review on Steam! - Farever Teamhttps://store.steampowered.com/app/3672400/Farever/

items.title: Online Fantasy RPG Farever’s New Endgame Arrives today with Call to Glory Update
Farever Early Access Review
items.summary: Farever Early Access review: A rough start hampered by performance. But there's a solid online action-RPG simmering just beneath the surface.
items.content:
Platform : PC (Steam Early Access) Developer : Shiro Games Publisher : Shiro Games

It’s easy to jump into the world of Farever . If you’ve played a modern-gen Zelda game , or Genshin Impact , or most open world RPGs, you already have a good idea how Farever plays: explore the world, battle monsters, find loot, and grow stronger. And do it all with others!

Farever doesn’t exactly break the genre mold, and the Early Access version is incredibly rough. But there’s a solid online action-RPG simmering just beneath the surface.

Read on for our Early Access Review of Farever !

At Early Access launch, Farever has four classes: Warrior, Mage, Priest, and Rogue. I usually play Rogues or Warriors in my fantasy RPGs, but this time I created a Mage. The class determines class skills, as well as which weapons I can wield. In the case of a mage, I use spellbooks, and my initial spellbook contains fire spells.

Like many RPGs, I begin on a beach, with very little fanfare. The online game knows I’m one of many adventurers; pretty much the opposite of a Chosen One. But I would’ve liked a bit more story context — and especially, an actual tutorial.

Farever does an incredibly poor job explaining its systems. While it’s true that too many games go overboard with hand-holding and tutorializing over their first dozen hours, Farever explains almost nothing. The game presumes I’ve played MMO-style fantasy RPGs before (I have), and simply sets me loose in its large world.

There’s always something interesting to check out

The beach is full of giant crabs, and my initial quest is to simply kill a bunch and turn in some of their claws. The most basic of MMO fetch quests.

Combat is entirely cooldown based. My basic attacks deal quick fire damage, while every third attack charges a more powerful blast. My main skill is a charged fireball. It deals a lot of damage and applies a burning effect, but it’s on a long cooldown. My second attack is much quicker, stunning enemies who are burning.

The strategy becomes simple but effective — begin each battle by launching a fireball. Then use my basic attack alongside the stun blast. Most similarly-leveled enemies die around the time they reach me, which is good because I’m quit squishy!

Boss battles where a whole different matter, however.

I quickly learned not to let this oversize boar hit me too many times

Thankfully I have a dodge, and as a mage I also learn a quick teleport dash, and a protective shield. Every class can also block to reduce damage, and reduce damage even further by timing it perfectly (a system I always appreciate).

items.content:
Gaming FAREVER Hits 100,000 Units Sold In First Week Of Early Access GameDaily Follow Franz Christian Irorita Fri, May 15, 2026 at 9:45 AM UTC Fri, May 15, 2026 at 9:45 AM UTC figure]:grid max-md:[&>figure]:grid-cols-article-mobile max-md:[&>figure>*]:col-fullbleed max-md:[&>figure>figcaption]:col-body"> *]:pointer-events-auto hidden md:block"> FAREVER Hits 100,000 Units Sold In First Week Of Early Access FAREVER is shaping up to be Shiro Games' latest hit. The online multiplayer action RPG that entered Early Access just a week ago has hit 100,00 units sold on Steam , off the back of its 175,000 wishlists when it was first revealed last year at the PC Gaming Show. It was indeed one of this year's most anticipated games .

FAREVER's online action role-playing game invites players to explore the fantasy world of Siagarta, either alone or with friends. FAREVER sports a colorful, cozy aesthetic that makes it more appealing to a wider audience, and its inviting look is already making it popular among gaming circles.

Not resting on their laurels, Shiro Games is promising continuous fixes and updates throughout the game's Early Access run, releasing its first patch this Wednesday.

"While we were confident that Farever 's world would resonate with adventurers, seeing them flock in droves to the Early Access launch has us even more excited about its future," says Shiro Games CEO Nicolas Cannasse. "Our goal is to create an immersive and enjoyable experience based on player feedback throughout Early Access, and we're committed to frequent updates over the coming months to make Farever event better."

This is necessary for the game's survival, too, as Farever currently sits at a measly 66% Mixed reviews on Steam. The silver lining? Almost 3,000 players left their impressions on the game's Steam reviews, indicating a strong community that really has an investment into this game's eventual success.

Shiro Games' roadmap for Farever includes additional regions, more enemy factions, World Events, increased difficulty modes, a Faction reputation system, an increased level cap, new classes and talent trees, more collection elements, new weapons and weapon skills, and social features such as a Guild System and PvP.
